title: Modifier discovery across trials: no penalty is both stable and powerful, and study-level heterogeneity creates a false modifier that more trials entrench
question: Are effect modifiers discovered from pooled trial data stable and correct enough to use, and do study-level confounders create false modifiers that more data do not remove?
design: Three to twelve trials at a fixed total of 2400 patients, one or three true modifiers among ten candidates, study-level confounding absent or present; pooled and within-trial lasso at two penalty rules; power, false discoveries, stability and target error. 12 cells, 300 replicates each.
answer: No. Lasso discovery at the minimum-error penalty found the true modifiers but added 1.7 to 2.8 false ones among seven null covariates, and sets from independent datasets agreed with Jaccard similarity 0.37 to 0.57; the one-standard-error rule was stable only by selecting nothing (a single modifier found in 3% to 5% of analyses). With an unmeasured study-level cause of effect heterogeneity, pooled discovery selected the covariate whose trial means tracked it in 69% of analyses with 3 trials and 93% with 12 at the same total size, and raised false discoveries among the other covariates from 1.7 to 2.8 per analysis to 3.6 to 3.9; trial-specific treatment effects removed both.
findings: Usability condition (stability at least 0.8 with at most 0.5 false modifiers in every cell) failed for every method and penalty.

Pooled minimum-error discovery selected the confounded covariate in 0.69, 0.81, 0.93 of analyses with 3, 6, 12 trials (one true modifier); within-trial discovery 0.14 to 0.46, the rate of any null covariate.
Pooled minimum-error target bias under confounding 0.023 to 0.057; one-standard-error rule biased toward no modification by 0.09 to 0.21.
not_answered: Lasso only (no multi-study causal forests); continuous outcome; linear modification; one overlap level; post-selection inference for the target not studied here. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Selection of true and false effect modifiers, stability of the selected set, and the target mean difference at covariate means 0.5
n_sim: 300 per cell, 12 cells, two datasets per replicate
